findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a single package of hamburgers in the prep cooler to be above 41F. The hamburger was probed at 51F by the PIC and then voluntarily thrown away. Ensure that food is held at or below 41F. For cooler notes, see violation 33.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be a cooler in the shop that was not holding food at or below 41F. Discussed with PIC and maintenance came and serviced the cooler while inspector and PIC were inspecting the Halfway House. Cooler has been serviced and is now holding at 41F. Ensure coolers are checked regularly to prevent food being stored too warm. For food notes, see violation 22.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the baffles of the ice machine have a build-up of soil and pink mold. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch. There will be a follow-up on 07/30/2024 to check that the baffles of the ice machine have been cleaned.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine baffle has some mold build-up.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on site.  Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly throughout the operating season.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

See violations #8 and #48.
- Multiple employees observed donning gloves without a handwash and several were observed using cell phones, putting hands in pockets, scratching face and hair while gloved. PIC observed coming into kitchen, donning gloves, and checking cell phone. Inspector pulled employees (6) aside and demonstrated a proper handwash and when to don gloves, and explained why this is important for food safety. Inspector advised that gloves are not to protect your hands, but to protect people's food when cooking, therefore should not be utilized unless preparing food. 

-When inspector inquired about location of sanitizer bucket, employees pointed at dispenser on the wall above the 3-part sink. Inspector clarified a working sanitizer bucket should be available to sanitize surfaces after spills or in between prep. Employee then grabbed a regular household bucket off the floor from underneath the handsink and began to fill it as a sanitizer bucket. Inspector asked employee to go to main house and get a sanitizer bucket that is cleaned and for sanitizer. Inspector provided education about when and how to use a sanitizer bucket and how to store rags in the establishment. Discussed with head chef Tom.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee enter into kitchen and don gloves without a proper handwash. Multiple employees (about 3) observed donning gloves upon inspector entry without a proper handwash and continue to do activities that contaminate gloves and hands (see #1). Inspector demonstrated proper handwashing procedure to employees at snack shop and provided education on importance of handwashing in regards to contamination and illness prevention.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

See #1. Sanitizer bucket not available in establishment. Employee created sanitizer bucket after education to a concentration of 400ppm.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) ice machine is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Lip of the ice machine observed to have pink slime building up. Discussed with the person in charge. Wash, rinse, and sanitizing lip piece will be added to the list of daily cleaning tasks.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.11  (Pf) Food-Contact surface is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

Cutting board at prep table in snack bar is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Replace cutting boards immediately.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Observed personal drinks in the following areas: bottle of iced tea in the food prep area and a bottle of mountain dew near the 3 compartment sink in the back of the kitchen. Ensure employees are provided a designated area for personal drinks away from or below food prep areas, with a lid and a straw, to prevent contamination. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11  (P) Bottle of simple syrup stored in the grill room bar is/are spoiled. All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. The syrup was discarded immediately. Reference 3-101.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Meat slicer was observed soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wall potato slicer was observed covered with debris and flies were circling the slicer. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Both meat slicer and potato slicer were cleaned during the inspection.
4-601.11(A) (Pf) Popcorn machine in grill area was observed coated in grease and other debris. Clean popcorn machine frequently between uses.
4-501.114  (P) Dish machines at both bar areas were not at proper sanitization (0ppm). Machine sanitizing was corrected during inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Sani bucket at upstairs bar and sani bucket at prep area had sanitizer concentrations of 50-100 ppm. Ensure sani buckets have a maintained concentration of 200ppm or greater during service hours. Corrected on sight.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on open milk and sour cream containers in the walk-in fridge. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded. 

Additionally, observed a smoked pimento cheese with a date mark of 3/26. Ensure foods prepared and held are discarded after seven days. Food was discarded.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly on top of ice bin underneath the spice rack. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at knife rack in food prep area. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Observed clean knives stored in the grooves behind the knife rack. Knives were removed and brought to the dish area for wash/sanitizing.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
1) Observed the milk in the bar area to be without a date designated when it was opened or when it needs to be discarded. The container was dated during the inspection. 2) Observed a quarter pan of chicken pot pie in the prep area's 4 door cooler at 46 F. Discussed with PIC and the item was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.
Observed shrimp thawing in a bucket of water in the 3 part ink to the back of the kitchen. Discussed with the PIC and the water was turned on to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Observed the machine used for slicing potatoes to have a large accumulation of food debris on it. Some of the debris was obviously from recent use and some was dried on from previous use. Discussed with the  PIC and instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves.

Observed a cup being used as a scoop for snack mix in the bar area. Scoops should have a handle that prevents hand contact with ready to eat foods. The cup was removed during the inspection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

Observed scoring on the cutting board that have accumulated soilage in the bar area. Discussed with the PIC and they stated that they would be removed.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.
Observed 1) the rim of the soda gun nozzle soiled with mold, 2) the popcorn maker in the men's grill soiled with food debris 3) the roof of the coffee maker soiled with splattered food debris. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to maintain the food contact surfaces clean in the facility.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Observed 1) crumbs on a shelf in the bread warmer in the wait station, 2) a shelf under the popcorn maker in the men's grill soiled with grease, 3) a dish caddy in the dish room soiled with food debris and 4) a fan blowing on clean dishes in the dish room soiled with dust. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to maintain clean.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

Observed 1) clean knives stored in containers with bottoms soiled with accumulated dust/ debris, 2) silverware in the wait station with accumulated debris. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean containers used for storing utensils regularly.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.
Observed 2 cans of mountain dew stored in the cooler on the back wall along with foods intended for customers. Discussed with the PIC and stated that an area should be designated for employee foods if desired.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
Employee stated marinara sauce is being heated, cooled, and reheated.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling. The facility is licensed as a medium risk. Cooling is considered a High risk process which is not allowed as a part of the licensing.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed unlabeled granola bar packaged in a sealed plastic bag located in the display cooler. Food items being sold for consumers must have proper labeling. 
750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed employee practicing improper hand washing techniques. All employees must practice good hand washing technique. This includes using a barrier to turn faucet off. 
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Turn off the sink with a clean barrier.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed debris on the grill surface.
2) Observed thermometer used for taking food temperatures to be soiled.
3) Observed spatula to be soiled and stored with clean utensils
All food contact surfaces must be cleaned and in proper repair. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed front ice-holding unit to have debris on top of the lid.
2) Observed slushie machine to be soiled with black debris.
All non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned as necessary to prevent possible contamination.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed utensils to be stored in soiled area. Clean utensils must be stored in a designated clean area.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single-use utensils being stored incorrectly. All tableware must be stored in a manner where handle is facing outward of the holder and easily accessible. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed ventilation near grill to be soiled. Ventilation must be clean and in good repair. 
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a container of unknown white powder above the prepping cooler. Provide a label on the container of unknown powder above the prepping cooler. An employee provided a label on the container of white powder above the prepping cooler to correct the violation during the routine inspection. •
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a single service cup used as a scooper in a container of white powder stored above the prepping cooler. Provide a scooper with a handle extending out of the powder. An employee removed the single service cup during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a wiping cloth laying under the smoothie machine. Store all sanitizer cloths in a properly concentrated sanitizer bucket when not in use. The wiping cloth was placed in a QT sanitizer bucket during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. •

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice machine deflector shield to be soiled with what appears to be slime and mold. Clean the ice machine deflector shield.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom of the mini freezer to be soiled with food debris. Clean the bottom mini freezer.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed a single service containers stored on the top of the prepping table with the food contact surface exposed. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak in the reach-in cooler. Repair the reach-in cooler.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed wiping cloths laying on the counters near the microwave. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer bucket or designated area. The employee removed the towel from the counter during the inpsection. The violation was corrected immediately.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed single service items not inverted on the top shelf above the microwave. Properly store the single service items. The employee properly stored the single service items. The violation was corrected during the inspection immediately.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towel in the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Provide paper towel in the paper towel dispenser.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed missing caulk behind the hand sink near the three compartment sink. Recaulk the hand sink to the wall near the three compartment sink.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - A) Open package of hotdogs in grill cooler and sliced tomatoes in top of prep cooler did not have date marks. Hotdogs and tomatoes were discarded in the trash.

B) Portions of deli meat in the bottom of the prep cooler had date marks of 14 and 15 (indicating 8/14 & 8/15). Other portions in the top of the prep cooler were dated 28, and the snack shop would not be open again until 9/4 (beyond 7 day time frame for use). All portions of deli meat were discarded in the trash.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food must be clearly dated and consumed, sold, or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. 
**Return unused portions of food to main kitchen or discard at close of business when operations will not occur for several days in a row (i.e. close on Sunday and don't plan to operate again until the following Friday).

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - A) Container  with raw chicken was stored over container of ready to eat food (deli meat portion) in the bottom of the prep cooler. Containers with chicken were placed beneath other products.

B) Open hotdogs were in the same drawer used to store a container of raw chicken in the grill cooler. 
Proper food storage was discussed with management. Hotdogs were discarded due to date marking (see #3a).

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Ice cream freezer had heavy ice/frost accumulation inside, and food debris was observed in the bottom. Defrost and clean the ice cream freezer.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test strip was not observe snack shop. Obtain and use quat test strips for checking sanitizer concentrations at the snack shop.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.
Quat = 200-400ppm

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Sleeves of single service cups were observed on the floor by the front counter. Sleeves were moved to storage shelf off the floor.

Single service articles shall be stored in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Drain hose for soda gun had black buildup inside. A fruit fly casing was observed in the hose. If the drain hose can not be thoroughly cleaned to remove buildup and fruit fly casing then replace the hose.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1130 - Trash can was half full; fruit flies were observed in the trash can. Trash and fruit flies were also observed in the small white bucket used as a trash receptacle at the front counter. Remove trash from the premise at the end of operations daily. 

Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - A) Ants were observed around the floor drain beneath the ice machine at the front counter. Clean the drain and eliminate potential food source for ants.

B) Hundreds of fruit flies were observed in the snack shop. Flies were observed around the soiled and clean dishes at the 3 part sink, in the soiled linen storage bag, in the garbage cans, in the microwave with food that was left inside, inside the spout of the soft serve machine, in a container of old soft serve beneath the spout, around the slushi machine, around the drain hose of the soda gun (casing - pupa stage between larva and adult - was observed in the soda gun drain hose. Soiled dishes were left from the last day of operation, and general surfaces throughout were soiled with food crumbs, splash, and general debris.
The snack shop must be thoroughly cleaned and the number of flies present must be significantly decreased prior to opening for Labor Day weekend. Utilize fly strips in addition to cleaning (beneath sinks and away from food, clean equipment, and single service articles).

Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - A) Floor drains were soiled with mold and general buildup.

B) Floor was soiled under equipment, especially under the cooking equipment (grease/food debris).

Clean the floor and the drains daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment:
750.1380b - Soiled linen bag was observed by 3 part sink and was noted to be a harborage location for fruit flies.

Remove soiled linen bag from facility daily/as needed for laundering.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Observed the floor drain under the 3-part sink and next to ice cream machine to be heavily soiled. Clean the floor and drain. 750-1220 Floor shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bottle to have no label. Sanitizer was labeled to correct the violations. 750-1300 Toxic items shall be labeled with their contents.
